after.RouteNotes: CB: route traced from published map — Route traced from the Yuma Pipeline overview map that FERC posted on August 28, 2026. The map is dated August 27, 2026, at a scale of 1 to 600,000. The red pipeline line was picked out of the image by its color and thinned to a one pixel centerline, so the trace follows every bend and corner of the printed line. It runs from milepost 0 near Buckeye to the Mexico border southwest of San Luis. The map was tied to real coordinates with 9 control points. Eight are county corners and border points from the US Census 2023 county boundary file. One is the Interstate 10 and Arizona Route 85 interchange at Buckeye, from OpenStreetMap. The fit error is about 0.1 km. As a check, the border drawn on the map lands within about 160 meters of the Census border. The mileposts printed on the map fall every 9.7 to 10.2 miles along the traced line. The traced line is about 137.2 miles long, against 138 miles stated for the project. The map is small scale and simplifies the line, so the route is rated medium. The map ends the line at the Mexico border, drawn into the middle of its thick border symbol, so the raw trace ran about 650 meters past the border. The line was cut at the United States border as drawn by Natural Earth, which the routes repository uses to check endpoints, and the last point sits 20 meters inside it. That end point is about 250 meters north of the Census border line. The September 2026 Federal Register scoping notice says the gas is mainly for northwest Mexico and the Yuma area.
